_about: SkillLens quiz bank. Multiple choice, 'answer' is the 0-based index of the correct option. Topics: python, csharp, sql, oop, algorithms.

questions.question: What does len([1, [2, 3], 4]) return?
questions.explanation: The list has three elements: 1, the nested list [2, 3], and 4. len counts top-level elements only.

questions.question: Which of these types is immutable?
questions.explanation: Tuples cannot be changed after creation; lists, dicts and sets can be modified in place.

questions.question: What is the result of 7 // 2 in Python 3?
questions.explanation: // is floor division, so 7 // 2 is 3. A single / would give 3.5.

questions.question: What does [x * 2 for x in range(4) if x % 2 == 0] produce?
questions.explanation: range(4) gives 0, 1, 2, 3; the filter keeps 0 and 2; doubling them gives [0, 4].

questions.question:
def f(a, items=[]):
    items.append(a)
    return items

What does f(1); f(2) return on the second call?
questions.explanation: Default arguments are evaluated once, when the function is defined, so the same list is reused across calls.

questions.question: Which keyword handles an exception raised inside a try block?
questions.explanation: Python uses try / except. catch is used in languages such as Java and C#.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of a 'with open(path) as f:' block?
options: It closes the file automatically, even if an error occurs
It opens the file in binary mode
It locks the file for other programs
questions.explanation: with uses a context manager; the file's __exit__ method closes it when the block ends, including on exceptions.

questions.question: What does d.get('k', 0) return when the dictionary d has no key 'k'?
questions.explanation: dict.get returns the default value (here 0) when the key is missing, instead of raising KeyError.

questions.question: What is printed by: a = [1, 2]; b = a; b.append(3); print(a)?
questions.explanation: b = a does not copy the list; both names refer to the same object, so the change is visible through a.

questions.question: What does a function containing 'yield' return when it is called?
options: A list of all yielded values
questions.explanation: Calling a generator function returns a generator; values are produced lazily when it is iterated.

questions.question: Which statement makes the function sqrt from the math module available as sqrt?
questions.explanation: The syntax is 'from module import name'.

questions.question: What is the value of 'python'[1:4]?
questions.explanation: Slicing includes the start index and excludes the end index: characters at 1, 2, 3 are 'y', 't', 'h'.

questions.question: What does the expression {1, 2, 3} & {2, 3, 4} evaluate to?
questions.explanation: & on sets is intersection: the elements present in both sets.

questions.question: Which C# type is a value type?
questions.explanation: int (System.Int32) is a struct, so it is a value type. string, object and List<T> are reference types.

questions.question: What does the 'var' keyword do in C#?
options: Lets the compiler infer the static type from the initialiser
questions.explanation: var is implicit typing: the type is still fixed at compile time, inferred from the right-hand side.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'const' and 'readonly' fields?
options: const is set at compile time; readonly can be set at runtime in a constructor
readonly is set at compile time; const can be set in a constructor
const can only be used for strings
questions.explanation: const values are compile-time constants; readonly fields are assigned at declaration or in the constructor.

questions.question: What does numbers.Where(n => n > 2).Select(n => n * 10) return for numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4}?
questions.explanation: Where keeps 3 and 4; Select multiplies each by 10.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'using' statement around an IDisposable object?
options: To call Dispose automatically when the block ends
questions.explanation: using (var x = ...) { } guarantees Dispose is called, even if an exception is thrown.

questions.question: Which access modifier makes a member visible only inside its own class?
questions.explanation: private restricts access to the containing type. protected also allows derived classes.

questions.question: What does 'await' do inside an async method?
options: Blocks the thread until the task finishes
Pauses the method without blocking the thread and resumes when the task completes
questions.explanation: await yields control back to the caller; the rest of the method runs as a continuation when the awaited task completes.

questions.question: What does 'int? x = null;' declare?
questions.explanation: T? on a value type is shorthand for Nullable<T>, which can hold null.

questions.question: A method is declared 'virtual' in a base class. What must a derived class use to replace its behaviour polymorphically?
questions.explanation: override replaces a virtual member so calls through a base reference use the derived implementation; new only hides it.

questions.question: Which collection stores key-value pairs with fast lookup by key?
questions.explanation: Dictionary is a hash table; lookups by key are O(1) on average.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a struct and a class in C#?
options: Structs are value types and are copied on assignment; classes are reference types
Structs are always allocated on the heap
questions.explanation: Assigning a struct copies its data; assigning a class instance copies the reference.

questions.question: Why is StringBuilder preferred over string concatenation inside a large loop?
options: string cannot be concatenated in loops
Strings are immutable, so each concatenation allocates a new string
questions.explanation: Each + on strings creates a new object; StringBuilder appends into a growing buffer.

questions.question: What does an interface in C# contain by default?
options: Member signatures that implementing classes must provide
questions.explanation: An interface defines a contract of members; classes that implement it provide the implementation (default interface methods are an optional later feature).

questions.question: Which clause filters rows before grouping?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.

questions.question: Which statement returns the number of rows in the table orders?
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows.

questions.question: What does a LEFT JOIN return?
options: Only rows that match in both tables
All rows from the left table, with matching right rows or NULLs
All rows from the right table only
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every left row; columns from the right table are NULL where no match exists.

questions.question: Which query lists each customer_id with its number of orders, only for customers with more than 5 orders?
options: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE COUNT(*) > 5 GROUP BY customer_id
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
SELECT customer_id FROM orders HAVING customer_id > 5
questions.explanation: Aggregates cannot be used in WHERE; conditions on groups go in HAVING.

questions.question: What does a PRIMARY KEY guarantee?
options: Values are unique and not NULL
The column is indexed as text
The column can reference another table
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL.

questions.question: Which condition correctly finds rows where email has no value?
questions.explanation: NULL is not equal to anything, not even NULL, so comparisons must use IS NULL.

questions.question: What is a FOREIGN KEY used for?
options: Linking a column to the primary key of another table to keep references valid
questions.explanation: A foreign key enforces referential integrity between related tables.

questions.question: Which keyword removes duplicate rows from a SELECT result?
questions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT returns each distinct row once.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an index on a column?
options: To speed up searches and joins on that column
To hide the column from queries
questions.explanation: Indexes let the database find rows without scanning the whole table, at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.

questions.question: What happens to all changes in a transaction when ROLLBACK is executed?
options: Only the last statement is undone
They are written to a log and kept
questions.explanation: ROLLBACK undoes every change made since the transaction began; COMMIT makes them permanent.

questions.question: What does UNION do, compared with UNION ALL?
options: UNION keeps duplicates, UNION ALL removes them
UNION removes duplicate rows, UNION ALL keeps them
UNION joins columns side by side
questions.explanation: UNION combines result sets and removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps every row and is faster.

questions.question: Why are parameterised queries used instead of building SQL strings from user input?
options: They run faster on every database
They prevent SQL injection by sending data separately from the SQL code
They avoid the need for indexes
questions.explanation: Parameters are never interpreted as SQL, so input such as ' OR 1=1 -- cannot change the query.

questions.question: Which clause sorts the result from highest to lowest salary?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY column DESC sorts in descending order; ASC (the default) sorts ascending.

questions.question: What is encapsulation?
options: Creating many objects from one class
Hiding internal state and exposing behaviour through a public interface
questions.explanation: Encapsulation keeps data private and controls access through methods, so invariants can be protected.

questions.question: Which relationship does inheritance usually model?
questions.explanation: A Dog is an Animal: inheritance models is-a. has-a is usually modelled with composition.

questions.question: What is polymorphism?
options: Calling the same method on different types and getting type-specific behaviour
questions.explanation: With polymorphism, code written against a base type works with any subtype, each providing its own implementation.

questions.question: What is an abstract class?
options: A class that cannot have methods
A class that cannot be instantiated directly and may contain abstract members
A class with only static members
questions.explanation: Abstract classes define shared behaviour and leave some members for subclasses to implement.

questions.question: What does 'favour composition over inheritance' recommend?
options: Build behaviour by combining objects instead of deep class hierarchies
Always inherit from at least two classes
questions.explanation: Composition keeps classes loosely coupled and lets behaviour change at runtime.

questions.question: What is a constructor?
options: A method that destroys an object
A special method that initialises a new object
questions.explanation: A constructor runs when an object is created and sets up its initial state.

questions.question: Which SOLID principle says a class should have only one reason to change?
questions.explanation: The Single Responsibility Principle keeps each class focused on one job.

questions.question: The Liskov Substitution Principle states that...
options: Subclasses should be usable anywhere their base class is expected without breaking correctness
Classes should depend on concrete implementations
Classes should be closed for extension
questions.explanation: If code works with a base type, it must also work with any subtype; a Square overriding Rectangle setters is a classic violation.

questions.question: Dependency Inversion suggests that high-level modules should depend on...
questions.explanation: Both high- and low-level code depend on abstractions, which makes it possible to swap implementations and test in isolation.

questions.question: Which design pattern ensures a class has only one instance?
questions.explanation: Singleton restricts instantiation to one object and provides a global access point.

questions.question: Which pattern lets objects subscribe to and be notified of changes in another object?
questions.explanation: In Observer, a subject keeps a list of observers and notifies them when its state changes.

questions.question: Which pattern selects an algorithm at runtime by passing in an object that implements a common interface?
questions.explanation: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind one interface.

questions.question: What is method overloading?
options: Redefining a base-class method in a subclass
Several methods with the same name but different parameter lists
Calling a method too many times
questions.explanation: Overloading is resolved at compile time by parameters; overriding replaces a base method at runtime.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the search range, so about log2(n) steps are needed.

questions.question: Which data structure follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) order?
questions.explanation: A stack removes the most recently added element first; a queue is FIFO.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of looking up a key in a hash table?
questions.explanation: Hashing maps a key directly to a bucket; with few collisions lookups are constant time on average.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of quicksort?
questions.explanation: With consistently bad pivots (for example an already sorted array and first-element pivot), quicksort degrades to O(n^2); its average is O(n log n).

questions.question: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph?
questions.explanation: BFS explores nodes level by level, so the first time it reaches a node is via a shortest path in edge count.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing the element at index i of an array?
questions.explanation: Array elements are stored contiguously, so the address of element i is computed directly.

questions.question: In a binary search tree, where are values smaller than a node stored?
questions.explanation: BST property: left subtree < node < right subtree, which makes in-order traversal sorted.

questions.question: Which technique stores results of subproblems to avoid recomputing them?
questions.explanation: Dynamic programming (memoisation or tabulation) reuses overlapping subproblem results, e.g. Fibonacci in O(n).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of merge sort in all cases?
questions.explanation: Merge sort always splits in half (log n levels) and merges in linear time per level.

questions.question: Which structure is best for always retrieving the smallest element quickly?
questions.explanation: A min-heap returns the minimum in O(1) and removes it in O(log n).

questions.question: Two nested loops, each running n times, have what time complexity?
questions.explanation: The inner body runs n * n times.

questions.question: What does a recursive function need to avoid infinite recursion?
options: A base case that stops the recursion
questions.explanation: Each recursive call must move towards a base case that returns without recursing.

questions.question: What is the cost of inserting at the head of a singly linked list?
questions.explanation: Only the new node's next pointer and the head pointer change, regardless of list length.
